While recent work on efficient reasoning reduces this overhead through length-based rewards or pruning, many approaches are post-trained under a much shorter context window than base-model training, a factor whose effect has not been systematically isolated. We first show that short-context post-training alone, using standa

summary.core_problem: 这篇论文研究高效推理 post-training 中一个容易混淆的因素：模型变短，究竟来自显式长度惩罚，还是来自短上下文 RL 训练本身。论文进一步处理短上下文训练带来的不稳定问题，尤其是正确中间推理被截断后拿到零奖励，从而被错误惩罚。
summary.importance: 这篇论文对预训练研究的价值在于连接了 base model 长上下文能力、post-training 上下文设置和推理长度分布。它提醒了一点：训练窗口本身就是很强的行为约束，不只是工程参数。短上下文 GRPO 会自然压缩 reasoning trace，但也会改变探索分布和 advantage 信号质量。这个观察对 cooldown、mid-training、RL 数据构造和长上下文能力保持都有参考价值。
summary.technical_approach: 论文先做了一个控制实验：对长上下文 reasoning model 使用短上下文的标准 GRPO，不加入长度奖励、token budget 或剪枝机制。结果显示，仅短上下文 post-training 就能产生接近已有高效推理方法的压缩效果。问题是 rollout 被上下文截断时，最终 verifier 给零奖励，GRPO 会把整条轨迹的 token 都分配负 advantage；其中不少中间步骤可能是正确的，这会产生噪声更新。Step-level Advantage Selection 将一条 reasoning trace 切成离散步骤，在步骤层面筛选 advantage。对正确 rollout 中低置信步骤置零 advantage，减少不可靠步骤被强化；对 verifier 失败 rollout 中高置信中间步骤置零 advantage，避免可能正确但因截断或 verifier 问题失败的步骤被惩罚。在 GRPO 的组内相对 advantage 归一化下，零 advantage 对正确样本相当于弱化，对失败样本相当于保护。
summary.experiments: 实验以 DeepScaleR-1.5B-Preview 为主要基座，在数学和通用推理 benchmark 上评估准确率与输出长度。相对基座模型，SAS 将平均输出长度降低超过 30%，同时平均 Pass@1 提升 1.51 个百分点。与 LAPO、ThinkPrune 等长度感知基线相比，SAS 在准确率更高的同时，平均生成 token 数少约 15%。论文还报告 Accuracy–Efficiency Score，在数学推理上相对最强对比方法有超过 0.13 的绝对提升。关键实验不是单点分数，而是短上下文纯 GRPO 的控制结果：它证明了上下文限制本身就是强压缩信号。
summary.reading_guide: 泛读 25–35 分钟。先看 Introduction 中关于短上下文 post-training 的控制问题，确认它和长度奖励方法的区别。方法部分重点看 SAS 如何在 GRPO 中把 rollout-level advantage 改成 step-level selection，以及零 advantage 在正确和失败样本中的非对称作用。实验部分重点看三类结果：短上下文纯 GRPO 的压缩与退化曲线，SAS 相对 LAPO、ThinkPrune 的 accuracy-length trade-off，以及关于截断 rollout 的分析。若关注 RL pretrain 或 reasoning model 的训练稳定性，建议细看训练动态曲线。

summary_en.core_problem: The paper isolates a confounder in efficient reasoning post-training: shorter reasoning may come not only from explicit length rewards, but also from training under a short context window. It then addresses the instability caused by this setup, where truncated but partially correct reasoning traces receive zero reward and can be penalized as if every step were wrong.
summary_en.importance: The useful point for foundation-model training is that context length is an optimization signal, not just an implementation setting. Short-context GRPO can compress reasoning without any length-aware reward, but it also distorts exploration and corrupts token-level credit assignment. This matters for RL post-training, long-context retention, cooldown schedules, and the design of verifiers for reasoning models.
summary_en.technical_approach: The paper first runs a controlled setup: a long-context reasoning model is post-trained with standard GRPO under a short context window, without length penalties, token budgets, or pruning. This alone produces substantial reasoning compression. The failure mode is credit assignment under truncation. In outcome-reward GRPO, a verifier-failed rollout receives a negative group-relative advantage across the whole sequence, even when many intermediate reasoning steps are valid. Step-level Advantage Selection treats reasoning as a sequence of steps and selectively zeros out advantages. In correct rollouts, low-confidence steps receive zero advantage so they are not reinforced. In verifier-failed rollouts, high-confidence intermediate steps receive zero advantage so they are protected from negative updates that may be caused by truncation or verifier errors. Because GRPO normalizes rewards within a group, a zero advantage weakens updates for questionable steps in correct traces and shields reliable steps in failed traces.
summary_en.experiments: The main experiments use DeepScaleR-1.5B-Preview and evaluate math plus general reasoning tasks. Compared with the base model, SAS reduces average output length by more than 30% while improving average Pass@1 by 1.51 points. Compared with length-aware baselines such as LAPO and ThinkPrune, it achieves higher accuracy with about 15% fewer generated tokens on average. The paper also reports an Accuracy–Efficiency Score gain of over 0.13 on math reasoning against the strongest competing methods. The most informative result is the control experiment showing that short-context GRPO by itself is a strong compression mechanism, but one that becomes unstable without step-level filtering.
summary_en.reading_guide: Skim in about 25–35 minutes. Start with the introduction’s control question: short-context training versus explicit length rewards. In the method section, focus on how SAS modifies rollout-level GRPO into step-level advantage selection and why zeroing advantages has different effects on correct and failed rollouts. In the experiments, prioritize the pure short-context GRPO curves, the accuracy-length trade-off against LAPO and ThinkPrune, and the analysis of truncated rollouts. Readers working on RL for reasoning models should spend extra time on the training-dynamics plots.

recommendation.zh: 值得看短上下文 GRPO 的隔离实验；若消融干净，会改变对“长度奖励才压缩推理”的默认看法。
recommendation.en: Read the short-context GRPO isolation study; if the ablations are clean, it weakens the default belief that length rewards are required to compress reasoning.

paper.title: JigsawRL: Assembling RL Pipelines for Efficient LLM Post-Training
paper.abstract: We present JigsawRL, a cost-efficient framework that explores Pipeline Multiplexing as a new dimension of RL parallelism. JigsawRL decomposes each pipeline into a Sub-Stage Graph that exposes the intra-stage and inter-worker imbalance hidden by stage-level systems. On this abstraction, JigsawRL resolves multiplexing interference through dynamic resource allocation, eliminates fragmented utilization by migrating long-tail rollouts across workers, and formulates their coordination as a graph sched

summary.core_problem: 在 LLM 的 RL post-training（含 agentic、多轮、工具调用等长尾 rollout）中，GPU 利用率长期偏低且随规模扩展出现“吞吐上升但成本更快上升”的问题。论文要解决的是：在多条并发 RL pipeline 共用集群时，如何通过更细粒度的建模与调度，把 rollout/training 内部与跨 worker 的不均衡转化为可优化的调度问题，从而提升单位成本吞吐。
summary.importance:
这不是预训练算法论文，但对“pretrain ↔ posttrain 闭环”的工程侧很相关：
- RL 迭代频繁、分支多，系统效率直接决定可探索的对齐/推理增强空间；
- 论文把瓶颈从“阶段级（rollout vs train）”下钻到“子阶段级”，并把多 pipeline 的空间复用作为一等公民，适合现实中共享集群/多实验并行的场景；
- 对研究者的启发点是：长尾序列与多轮交互导致的碎片化，单靠异步或 time-mux 很难根治，需要显式建模子阶段的 compute/memory 互补性与样本迁移。
局限：主要贡献在系统调度与资源管理，不涉及新的 RL 目标或收敛性质；对纯预训练方法研究的直接增益有限。
summary.technical_approach:
JigsawRL 的核心抽象是 Sub-Stage Execution Graph：把传统 RL pipeline 的粗粒度 stage（rollout、training 等）拆成更细的 sub-stage，并显式标注每个 sub-stage 的计算/显存特征与依赖关系，从而暴露两类隐藏不均衡：
1) intra-stage：rollout 内部由于 prefill/decoding、多轮交互、外部工具等待造成的时间片碎片；
2) inter-worker：不同 DP worker 因长尾样本导致进度不一致。

在该图抽象上做两类操作：
- Sub-stage Multiplexing：在多条并发 pipeline 之间，把 compute-heavy 与 memory-heavy 的 sub-stage 交错执行，并动态分配资源以减少互相干扰（避免静态切分导致的 contention 或空转）。
- Sub-stage Merging：针对长尾 rollout 造成的“某些 worker 拖尾、其他 worker 空闲”，通过迁移长尾样本/rollout 任务在 DP 实例间做合并与再平衡，减少碎片化执行。

调度求解被表述为图调度问题，使用 look-ahead heuristic 在关键路径上协调 multiplexing 与 merging，目标是提升吞吐/成本比而非单纯 wall-clock。
summary.experiments:
在 4–64 张 H100/A100 上，覆盖三类 agentic RL pipeline 与六个模型设置，报告的吞吐提升为：
- 同步 RL：最高 1.85× 相对 Verl；
- 异步 RL：最高 1.54× 相对 StreamRL 与 AReaL。
论文还通过 profiling 指出基线系统的平均 MFU 常低于 10%，且 GPU 数增加时 MFU 进一步下降；主要瓶颈来自 rollout 长尾与多轮/工具调用带来的不确定时延。

从你给的正文片段看，更多细节（具体 pipeline 组成、各子阶段的资源曲线、迁移开销、对收敛/稳定性的影响）需要到实验与系统实现章节看完整图表与 ablation。
summary.reading_guide:
泛读建议（30–45 分钟）：
1) 先看 Motivation 的 profiling 图：理解 MFU 低与长尾 rollout 的来源（prefill/decoding、多轮、工具等待）。
2) 直接跳到 Sub-Stage Graph 定义与两个关键机制（multiplexing/merging），把“为什么 stage-level 看不到问题”看明白。
3) 看实验主表：对比 Verl/StreamRL/AReaL 的吞吐提升，并留意在不同 GPU 数、不同 pipeline 下增益是否稳定。

如果你在做 RLHF/GRPO/RLAIF 的系统搭建：重点关注 sample migration 的实现代价（权重同步/通信/一致性）以及 look-ahead 调度对尾延迟的改善幅度。

summary_en.core_problem: RL post-training pipelines for LLMs—especially agentic, multi-turn, tool-using workloads—suffer from severe GPU underutilization driven by long-tailed rollouts and synchronization/imbalance across workers. The paper targets cost efficiency: how to multiplex multiple concurrent RL pipelines on shared GPU clusters by modeling fine-grained execution and scheduling resources to reduce fragmentation.
summary_en.importance:
This is a systems paper (not a pretraining-method paper), but it matters for the pretrain–posttrain loop in practice:
- RL is iterative and produces many model variants; system efficiency directly affects how much alignment/reasoning exploration is feasible.
- The key insight is that stage-level abstractions (rollout vs training) hide the real imbalance; sub-stage modeling plus cross-pipeline spatial multiplexing can fill idle periods better than purely async execution or time-mux.
- It also highlights a recurring issue for long-context/agentic training: long-tail sequence distributions create fragmentation that requires explicit task migration and scheduling.
Limitations: it does not propose new RL objectives or convergence theory; the contribution is primarily scheduling/resource management.
summary_en.technical_approach:
JigsawRL introduces a Sub-Stage Execution Graph that decomposes coarse RL stages into finer sub-stages with explicit compute/memory profiles and dependencies, exposing (1) intra-stage fragmentation within rollout (prefill/decoding interleaving, multi-turn interactions, tool-wait idle time) and (2) inter-worker imbalance from long-tail samples.

On top of this graph, it performs:
- Sub-stage multiplexing: co-schedule sub-stages from different pipelines, leveraging complementary compute vs memory demands, with dynamic resource allocation to mitigate interference.
- Sub-stage merging: migrate long-tail rollout samples/tasks across DP instances to reduce tail-induced fragmentation and rebalance workers.

Coordination is formulated as a graph scheduling problem solved with a look-ahead heuristic along the critical path, optimizing throughput per cost rather than only wall-clock time.
summary_en.experiments:
Evaluated on 4–64 H100/A100 GPUs across three agentic RL pipelines and six model settings:
- Up to 1.85× throughput over Verl for synchronous RL.
- Up to 1.54× throughput over StreamRL and AReaL for asynchronous RL.
The paper reports baseline MFU often below 10%, worsening with more GPUs, and attributes the inefficiency mainly to long-tailed rollouts and stochastic multi-turn/tool-calling behaviors.

More detailed ablations (sub-stage breakdowns, migration overhead, impact on training stability) should be taken from the full experiment/implementation sections beyond the provided excerpt.
summary_en.reading_guide:
Skim plan (30–45 min):
1) Read the profiling/motivation figures to internalize where utilization is lost (tail latency, multi-turn, tool waits).
2) Focus on the Sub-Stage Graph definition and the two mechanisms (multiplexing and merging); this is the conceptual core.
3) Check the main throughput tables against Verl/StreamRL/AReaL and whether gains persist across GPU counts and heterogeneous pipelines.

If you operate RLHF/GRPO/RLAIF infrastructure, pay special attention to sample migration costs (communication, weight transfer) and how the look-ahead scheduler reduces tail effects.

recommendation.zh: 读系统抽象和调度实验即可；若内部 RL 训练已被 rollout 长尾卡住，值得复现调度策略。
recommendation.en: Read the system abstraction and scheduling results; if rollout tails dominate your RL stack, the scheduling policy is worth reproducing.

paper.title: Hierarchical Policy Optimization for Simultaneous Translation of Unbounded Speech
paper.abstract: Simultaneous speech translation (SST) generates translations while receiving partial speech input. Recent advances show that large language models (LLMs) can substantially improve SST quality, but at the cost of high computational overhead. To reduce this cost, prior work reformulates SST as a multi-turn dialogue task, enabling full reuse of the LLM's key-value (KV) cache and eliminating redundant feature recomputation. However, this approach relies on supervised fine-tuning (SFT) data in dialog

summary.core_problem: 这篇工作处理的是流式同声传译里的一个很具体但很棘手的问题：如何在长时、无界语音输入下，同时兼顾翻译质量、时延和推理效率。已有路线把 SST 改写成多轮对话式的 read–write 生成，从而复用语音编码器和 LLM 的 KV cache，推理上很省，但训练依赖合成的交错轨迹数据。这类轨迹往往带噪声：词对齐法不理解未来上下文，LLM 分段法又不保证 read/write 决策合法。结果是模型会学到错误的等待或抢跑行为。论文的核心问题不是再造一个新架构，而是如何在 imperfect SFT 之后，用一个稳定的后训练方法把策略纠偏，而且不能让“低时延”这个容易优化的目标压过“翻译正确”这个更难目标。
summary.importance: 对基座研究的直接价值不在 SST 任务本身，而在训练信号设计。它给了一个很清楚的例子：当多目标优化里不同 reward 的难度和梯度形态差很多时，简单加权和往往会把策略推向错误方向。这里 latency reward 很容易被模型投机性利用，只要更早输出就能拿分，但质量会掉。作者用层级式 reward 把“先过质量门槛，再谈时延”写进优化目标，这比调一个静态权重更接近真实偏好约束。这个思路对 RLHF、推理模型 post-training、以及任何 accuracy–cost / quality–latency 联合优化问题都有参考意义。贡献量级上，它更像一个扎实的训练方法改进，而不是范式变化；但在“如何让 RL 修正有噪 SFT 数据”这件事上，信息密度是够的。
summary.technical_approach:
方法建立在 InfiniSST 架构上：前端是流式语音编码器，按 chunk 增量编码并复用历史 KV；后端是 LLM 翻译器，输入是交错的语音特征和已生成文本，遇到 <EOT> 就结束当前 chunk 的输出。为了支持无界长语音，语音侧用 sliding window，LLM 侧配 Attention Sink。训练上先用合成的 interleaving 数据做 SFT，再做 HPO 后训练。

HPO 的主体是对 GRPO 的改造。对每个长语音片段，策略采样多个候选翻译轨迹，分别计算质量奖励和时延奖励。关键不在“用了 GRPO”，而在 reward 结构：
1. 质量奖励和时延奖励分开计算，而不是先线性合并。
2. 设一个质量阈值；如果某条轨迹的质量没过线，则其 latency reward 直接打到最小值。这样模型不能靠提前输出换取总 reward。
3. 对质量和时延 reward 分别做 group normalization，再合并成最终优势信号，减少某一项 reward 方差或尺度主导训练。

这个设计针对的是 SST 的结构性难点。时延目标天然单调，容易学成“尽早说”；质量目标则稀疏、延迟、且受整句一致性影响。层级 reward 相当于把优化从“软权衡”改成“带门控的偏好约束”。从全文表述看，作者还强调这是在有噪轨迹监督上的纠偏，而不是从零学 read/write policy，因此它依赖一个还算可用的 SFT 初始化。论文也说明了训练样本构造：从分钟到小时级长录音中切出最长 67.2 秒的片段，每段 60 个 chunk、每个 chunk 1.12 秒；先用 ASR 时间戳对齐语音和转写，再用 SimAlign 做 transcript–translation 对齐，生成交错格式数据。
summary.experiments:
实验主要在 ACL 60/60 dev 和 RealSI 上做，关注的是不同平均时延下的翻译质量。摘要里给出的代表性结果是：在平均时延 1.5 秒时，相比最强基线，HPO 带来 +7 COMET、+1.25 MetricX、+4 BLEURT 的提升。这说明它不是只在某个单一指标上讨巧，而是在多种质量评测上都改善。

从全文设定看，实验重点应包括三类比较：
1. 与仅 SFT 的 InfiniSST 比较，验证后训练是否能修正合成轨迹噪声带来的策略偏差。
2. 与直接把质量和时延做平权或简单加权的 RL 目标比较，验证层级 reward 的必要性。
3. 与不同 latency operating points 的比较，证明改进不是只出现在高时延或低时延某一端，而是在较宽时延区间都成立。

论文最有价值的消融通常在 reward 设计上：去掉质量阈值门控后，模型会更倾向于抢跑；不做分项 group normalization 时，训练更不稳，或者某一 reward 主导更新。由于给出的全文片段没有完整表格，无法逐项复述所有数字，但主结论很明确：HPO 在固定时延下提升质量，在质量相近时也能压低时延，而且这种收益出现在长时流式场景而不是短句离线翻译。
summary.reading_guide:
泛读时先抓三处。

第一，看 Introduction 和 Figure 1，弄清作者为什么坚持 dialogue-style SST。重点不是任务背景，而是 KV cache 复用如何把长时流式翻译做成可扩展的生成问题。

第二，看 HPO 方法部分和 Figure 2。这里要重点理解两件事：为什么 latency reward 比 quality reward 更容易被优化；为什么“质量不过线则时延记最差”比简单加权更合理。若只看公式而不看动机，很容易把它误读成普通 reward shaping。

第三，看实验里的 reward ablation 和 latency-quality tradeoff 图。这里最能看出方法是否真的在纠偏，而不是单纯把 operating point 往高时延方向推。

如果只是判断是否值得跟进，30 分钟足够：读引言、方法图、主结果表和 reward 消融。若关心 RL for noisy supervision，可再细看训练细节、阈值设定、group normalization 的实现位置，以及不同评测指标之间是否一致。

summary_en.core_problem: The paper tackles a specific but important failure mode in simultaneous speech translation under long, effectively unbounded audio streams: how to improve translation quality and latency jointly when the model is trained on noisy synthesized read/write trajectories. Recent SST systems reformulate the task as an interleaved dialogue so they can fully reuse KV cache across speech and text, which is attractive for long-context streaming inference. The problem is that the supervision used to train those read/write behaviors is imperfect. Alignment-based synthesis ignores future context needed for proper timing, while LLM-based segmentation does not guarantee valid trajectories. As a result, the model learns brittle waiting and premature-writing behaviors. The paper asks how to correct those behaviors in post-training without letting the easy-to-optimize latency objective dominate the harder quality objective.
summary_en.importance: Its value for foundation-model researchers is less about SST as an application and more about multi-objective RL under uneven reward difficulty. The paper gives a clean case where a naive weighted sum is structurally misaligned with the desired behavior: latency reward is easy to game, because emitting earlier often improves the score even when translation quality degrades. The proposed hierarchical reward encodes a preference constraint directly: quality must clear a threshold before latency can matter. That idea is relevant beyond speech translation, especially for RLHF-style settings, reasoning-model post-training, and any quality-cost or quality-latency optimization where one reward is much easier to exploit than another. This is not a new modeling paradigm, but it is a solid training-design contribution on how RL can repair noisy SFT supervision.
summary_en.technical_approach:
The system is built on InfiniSST. A streaming speech encoder processes incoming chunks incrementally while reusing past KV states. An LLM translator then consumes interleaved speech features and previously generated text, and emits a partial translation for each chunk until it outputs an <EOT> token. For unbounded streams, the encoder uses a sliding window and the LLM uses Attention Sink to remain tractable over long contexts. Training proceeds in two stages: supervised fine-tuning on synthesized interleaving trajectories, followed by the proposed Hierarchical Policy Optimization.

HPO is an adaptation of GRPO. For each long-form speech segment, the policy samples multiple candidate translation trajectories. Each trajectory is evaluated with two rewards: translation quality and latency. The main contribution is not simply applying GRPO, but restructuring the reward:
1. Quality and latency are computed separately rather than merged upfront.
2. A quality threshold is imposed. If a sampled trajectory does not exceed that threshold, its latency reward is forced to the minimum. This prevents the policy from collecting reward by translating too early.
3. Group normalization is applied separately to the quality and latency rewards before they are combined, which reduces instability from scale mismatch and prevents one reward from dominating the update.

This design matches the asymmetry of the task. Latency is monotonic and easy to optimize in the wrong way; quality is delayed, sparse, and depends on global consistency. The hierarchical reward turns a soft trade-off into a gated preference structure. The paper also makes clear that this is a correction mechanism on top of a usable SFT initialization, not a from-scratch policy-learning setup. The synthesized training data are built from long recordings ranging from minutes to hours, segmented into windows up to 67.2 seconds, with 60 chunks of 1.12 seconds each; ASR timestamps align speech to transcripts, and SimAlign is used for transcript-translation alignment.
summary_en.experiments:
Experiments are run on the ACL 60/60 development set and RealSI, focusing on translation quality at different average latency levels. The headline result reported in the paper is that at 1.5 seconds average latency, HPO improves over the strongest baseline by +7 COMET, +1.25 MetricX, and +4 BLEURT. That matters because the gain is not confined to a single metric.

From the full setup, the most important comparisons are:
1. HPO versus the SFT-only InfiniSST baseline, to test whether post-training can repair errors induced by noisy synthesized trajectories.
2. HPO versus simpler RL objectives that combine quality and latency with a flat weighting, to show why the hierarchical reward is necessary.
3. Performance across a range of latency operating points, to verify that the method improves the quality-latency frontier rather than merely shifting the model toward slower decoding.

The most informative ablations are on reward design. Removing the quality gate should make the model more eager to emit prematurely. Removing separate group normalization should make training less stable or let one reward dominate. The provided excerpt does not include all tables, so not every number can be reproduced here, but the main empirical message is clear: HPO improves quality at fixed latency and can also reduce latency at comparable quality, in long-form streaming settings rather than short offline translation.
summary_en.reading_guide:
For a quick pass, focus on three parts.

First, read the introduction and Figure 1 to understand why the authors insist on dialogue-style SST. The key point is not the application setup itself, but how KV-cache reuse turns long-form streaming translation into a scalable generation problem.

Second, read the HPO section and Figure 2 carefully. The central question is why latency reward is easier to optimize than quality reward, and why “quality first, then latency” is better encoded as a gated reward than as a weighted sum. If you only read the equations, it can look like ordinary reward shaping, which misses the point.

Third, inspect the latency-quality tradeoff plots and reward ablations. Those are the places where you can tell whether the method truly corrects policy behavior rather than simply moving to a higher-latency regime.

If the goal is triage, about 30 minutes is enough: introduction, method figure, main result table, and reward ablations. If you care about RL under noisy supervision, spend more time on the threshold choice, where normalization is applied, and whether the gains are consistent across evaluation metrics.

recommendation.zh: 值得看奖励设计：把“延迟”做成可优化的层级信号而不是硬约束；只读奖励定义与消融，别被同传应用细节带跑偏。
recommendation.en: Read for the reward design: latency as an optimizable hierarchical signal rather than a hard constraint; focus on reward/ablations, not the SST application details.

paper.title: Evaluating the Progression of Large Language Model Capabilities for Small-Molecule Drug Design
paper.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have the potential to accelerate small molecule drug design due to their ability to reason about information from diverse sources and formats. However, their practical utility remains unclear due to the lack of benchmarks that reflect real-world scenarios. In this work, we introduce a suite of chemically-grounded tasks spanning molecular property prediction, molecular representation transformations, and molecular design. Importantly, we formulate these tasks as reinf

summary.core_problem: 评估 LLM 在小分子药物设计任务上的真实能力边界，并检验基于环境反馈的 RL 后训练能否显著提升化学任务表现。
summary.importance: 贡献主要是化学任务 benchmark 与 RL 环境化评测框架，同时给出一个对后训练研究有用的信号：在专业领域、低数据设定下，RL post-training 可以让小模型逼近前沿大模型。它不是预训练论文，但对 pretrain↔posttrain 接口有一定参考价值。
summary.technical_approach: 构建一组 chemically-grounded 任务，覆盖分子性质预测、分子表示转换和分子设计，并统一表述为 RL 环境，既可做评测也可做后训练。随后在三个模型家族上比较基础能力，并用 RL-based post-training 检验性能增益。
summary.experiments: 摘要称覆盖三个模型家族，发现 frontier models 的化学能力在提升，但低数据实验仍明显不足；更关键的是，经过 RL 后训练的小模型可与当前前沿模型竞争。摘要未给出参数量、训练 token、具体 baseline 名称和提升幅度，因此结论更适合作为方向性信号而非定量定论。
summary.authors_note: John Bradshaw 是机器学习与科学建模方向较知名研究者，长期关注分子生成与科学机器学习；其参与使这篇工作在科学任务设定上相对可信。

summary_en.core_problem: The paper measures the real capability boundary of LLMs for small-molecule drug design and tests whether RL-based post-training can materially improve performance on chemistry-grounded tasks.
summary_en.importance: Its main contribution is a chemistry benchmark framed as RL environments, plus an empirically useful post-training signal: in specialized, low-data regimes, RL post-training can make smaller models competitive with frontier models. It is not a pretraining paper, but it is relevant to the pretrain–posttrain interface.
summary_en.technical_approach: The authors build a suite of chemically grounded tasks spanning molecular property prediction, representation transformation, and molecular design, and cast them uniformly as RL environments for both evaluation and post-training. They then compare three model families and apply RL-based post-training to test gains.
summary_en.experiments: The abstract reports evaluations across three model families, finding that frontier models are improving on chemistry tasks but still struggle in low-data settings. More notably, a smaller model after RL post-training becomes competitive with state-of-the-art frontier models. The abstract does not provide parameter counts, training tokens, exact baselines, or effect sizes, so the result should be treated as directional rather than definitive.
summary_en.authors_note: John Bradshaw is a recognizable researcher in ML for molecules and scientific modeling, which makes the task design and scientific framing more credible.

recommendation.zh: 不是基座论文，但“RL 环境化专业任务能把小模型拉近大模型”这个信号值得记；只看任务设计和 post-train 对比表，别在化学细节里耗时。
recommendation.en: Not a base-model paper, but the signal that RL environments can let smaller models close the gap in specialized domains is worth noting; read the task setup and post-training tables only.

paper.title: Agent^2 RL-Bench: Can LLM Agents Engineer Agentic RL Post-Training?

summary.core_problem: 论文要回答的问题是：LLM 智能体能否在受限工程预算内，端到端“工程化”完成 agentic RL post-training（从目标理解、方案选择、代码实现/调参/排错、到在线采样闭环训练与多次提交），并真实提升给定基座模型的可测评性能；以及现有偏静态的后训练/自动化基准为何会高估这种能力。
summary.importance: RL 后训练已成为对齐与专精的关键路径，但真正落地需要跨奖励设计、算法选择、稳定性、数据/轨迹管线、在线交互与诊断迭代等系统工程能力。若智能体能自动化该流程，将显著降低模型研发门槛；反之，若基准只测“写出训练脚本/做 SFT”，就无法评估智能体是否具备构建可运行在线 RL 系统的能力，因此需要覆盖训练结构的交互式评测与可诊断的行为记录。
summary.technical_approach:
提出 Agent^2 RL-Bench：以“训练结构覆盖（training structure coverage）”为核心设计原则，构造 6 个任务、3 个难度层级的基准来逐级增加结构性要求。每个实例由任务描述D、基座模型M0、训练数据T、评测oracle O、时间预算τ定义；智能体A在预算内可迭代实现训练、提交候选模型并以“预算内最佳提交”的提升幅度作为得分（相对M0的 improvement）。
Level 1：静态、规则可验证任务（如 GSM8K、HumanEval），主要考察数据构造与监督训练闭环；
Level 2：静态但基于 judge 的非确定性奖励（如 AlpacaEval），要求对噪声/非确定信号进行优化；
Level 3：强交互任务（ALFWorld、WebShop、DeepSearchQA），必须实现环境交互、轨迹采集、基于轨迹级奖励的闭环在线 RL，并在固定 12 小时预算内迭代。
此外，基准强调“行为诊断”：为每次运行提供隔离工作区与 grading API；运行时 instrumentation 记录每次提交、代码修订、模型产物；并用事后分析模块自动生成结构化 case study 与 run report，用于分析智能体如何搜索、失败与自适应，而不仅是最终分数。
summary.experiments:
作者在受控实验中评估 5 套 agent 系统（跨 3 类 scaffold）与 6 个 driver LLM（如 OpenHands、OpenCode、Claude Code、Codex CLI、Gemini CLI）。主要发现：
1）在部分交互任务上可获得巨大增益：例如 ALFWorld 上，一个“RL-only”智能体通过 SFT warm-up + GRPO + 在线 rollouts，将分数从 5.97 提升到 93.28，显示智能体在特定环境中能搭建有效闭环。
2）但在其他交互任务上进展有限：如 DeepSearchQA 仅 +2.75，接近评测噪声，暴露在线 RL 工程稳定性与有效性难以复现。
3）在固定 scaffold 内更换 driver 会显著改变结果：在 Qwen3-8B-Base 的受控研究中，ALFWorld 的提升可从接近 0 变为 +78 个百分点，提示“driver 选择/能力”对交互式后训练成败影响很大。
4）总体上，在固定预算下，监督式管线往往主导最终最优路线；在线 RL 作为最终最佳路径只在 ALFWorld 上稳定胜出，说明“会写 RL 代码”与“能跑通 RL 系统并稳定提升”之间存在系统性鸿沟。
summary.reading_guide:
skim（泛读建议：方法概述+看点）：
- 重点读 Introduction：理解为何静态基准会高估能力、以及 Level 1→3 的结构递进逻辑。
- 读“Benchmark formulation/score=improvement + best-within-budget”相关段落：把握评测协议与迭代提交机制。
- 快看实验结论段：ALFWorld 的大幅提升 vs DeepSearchQA 的边际提升，以及“driver 影响巨大”的结论。

must_read（精读建议：详细技术分析+看点）：
- 精读基准定义部分：实例五元组(D,M0,T,O,τ)、迭代提交与 run-level best score 的设计动机（贴近真实后训练工作流）。
- 精读 Level 1/2/3 的“结构性要求”差异：
  1) Level 1 的确定性验证如何让 SFT 足以拿高分；
  2) Level 2 的 judge 噪声如何改变优化问题（非确定奖励下的策略选择与稳定性）；
  3) Level 3 对 rollout/trajectory reward/online collection 的硬约束如何逼出系统工程能力。
- 精读“runtime instrumentation + post-hoc analysis”设计：它如何把一次 run 的代码/模型/提交序列转化为可复盘的行为证据（对诊断 agent 策略尤关键）。
- 精读受控 scaffold–driver 实验：理解作者如何隔离变量、以及为何得出“driver 决定交互任务成败”的证据链。
- 创新点抓手：训练结构覆盖的任务选择原则；best-within-budget 的迭代评测协议；全程工件记录与自动化 run report（让 benchmark 不止是 leaderboard，而是行为科学仪器）。
summary.authors_note: 作者的核心立场是：仅靠静态/半静态后训练基准无法评估“工程化在线 RL”的真实能力；必须引入需要环境交互与轨迹闭环的任务，并配套可观测、可复盘的行为记录与分析。实验上他们既展示了智能体在个别环境可实现惊人提升，也强调这种成功并不稳健、强依赖完整 agent stack（尤其 driver），从而揭示当前智能体距离可靠自动化 RL 系统工程仍有明显差距。

summary_en.core_problem: The paper asks whether LLM agents can autonomously engineer end-to-end agentic RL post-training under a limited engineering budget—i.e., understand objectives, choose methods, implement/debug full pipelines (including online rollouts and trajectory-level rewards), iteratively submit models, and measurably improve a given foundation model—while diagnosing why existing mostly-static benchmarks can overestimate this capability.
summary_en.importance: RL post-training increasingly drives alignment and specialization, but real-world deployment requires expert system engineering across reward design, algorithm choice, stability, data/trajectory pipelines, and online interaction. If agents could automate this loop, they would become powerful model-development tools. However, benchmarks that can be solved largely by SFT do not test interactive RL engineering; thus, an evaluation must cover training-structure requirements and provide behavioral observability beyond final scores.
summary_en.technical_approach:
Agent^2 RL-Bench is introduced with a “training structure coverage” principle: 6 tasks across 3 levels, each level adding a structural requirement not present before. Each instance is defined by (task description D, base model M0, training data T, evaluation oracle O, time budget τ). Within τ, an agent A can iteratively implement training, run experiments, and submit candidate models via a grading API; the run score is the best improvement over M0 achieved within budget (best-within-budget), mirroring real post-training iteration.
Level 1: static rule-based tasks with deterministic verification (e.g., GSM8K, HumanEval) to test data construction + supervised training.
Level 2: static but judge-based, non-deterministic rewards (e.g., AlpacaEval), requiring optimization under noisy signals.
Level 3: fully interactive environments (ALFWorld, WebShop, DeepSearchQA) requiring environment interaction, trajectory collection, and closed-loop online RL within a fixed 12-hour budget.
For diagnosis, the benchmark provides isolated workspaces, runtime instrumentation that logs every submission/code revision/model artifact, and a post-hoc analysis module that auto-generates structured case studies and run reports—enabling analysis of how agents search, fail, and adapt.
summary_en.experiments:
Across controlled experiments with five agent systems (three scaffold families) and six driver LLMs (e.g., OpenHands, OpenCode, Claude Code, Codex CLI, Gemini CLI), results show:
1) Large interactive gains can occur on some tasks: on ALFWorld, an RL-only agent improves from 5.97 to 93.28 using SFT warm-up + GRPO with online rollouts.
2) Progress can be marginal on others: DeepSearchQA improves only +2.75, within evaluation noise, indicating difficulty in reliably engineering stable online RL.
3) Driver choice can dominate outcomes: in a controlled study on Qwen3-8B-Base, switching drivers within the same scaffold changes ALFWorld improvement from near-zero to +78pp.
4) Under fixed budgets, supervised pipelines often dominate; online RL emerges as the final best route reliably only on ALFWorld—highlighting a gap between writing RL code and running effective RL systems.
summary_en.reading_guide:
skim (high-level + what to read):
- Read the Introduction for the motivation: why static benchmarks overstate post-training competence and why Level 1→3 is diagnostic.
- Read the benchmark protocol: improvement-over-base and best-within-budget iterative submissions.
- Skim the main experimental findings: ALFWorld’s dramatic gains vs DeepSearchQA’s marginal gains, plus the “driver matters a lot” takeaway.

must_read (deep technical + what to focus on):
- Study the formal instance definition (D, M0, T, O, τ) and the best-within-budget scoring rationale.
- Carefully compare Level 1/2/3 structural requirements:
  (i) deterministic verification where SFT can suffice,
  (ii) judge-noise optimization in Level 2,
  (iii) mandatory rollout/trajectory-reward/online collection in Level 3.
- Deep-read the instrumentation + post-hoc analysis design: how full run artifacts become behavioral evidence.
- Deep-read the controlled scaffold–driver experiment to understand the causal claim that driver choice strongly affects interactive RL engineering.
- Key innovations to track: training-structure coverage as benchmark design; iterative best-within-budget evaluation; full run logging + automated run reports for behavioral diagnosis.
summary_en.authors_note: The authors argue that static or semi-static post-training benchmarks are insufficient to evaluate true online RL engineering competence. Meaningful evaluation requires interactive environments plus instrumentation for behavioral diagnosis. Their experiments intentionally show both extremes—spectacular success on ALFWorld and near-failure elsewhere—and emphasize that success depends on the full agent stack (especially the driver), revealing a persistent gap between generating RL code and reliably operating RL systems end-to-end.
